_note: Pre-run plan for exp-040 (query masking re-run on the v2 pipeline). Written before any run; nothing in this file is a measured exp-040 result. The per-run snapshots the runner writes (runs/exp-040/<arm>/decomposer/<ts>/config.json) are the record of what actually ran and are copied here after the run. ONE factor moves between arms: which masked form of the question the few-shot retrieval matches on (--retrieval-mode raw | uniform | typed). The prompt always shows the RAW query and the RAW exemplar questions (run_decomposer.examples_from_reranked_row reads pool_question), so masking changes only WHICH 5 exemplars are retrieved. Model, 4-bit precision, condition, pool, retriever (e5-small-v2 top-20 -> ms-marco-MiniLM-L-12-v2 top-5), few-shot ordering, decoding, seed, step parser and evaluation set are exp-020's. experiments/exp-040/run.sh and notebooks/exp-040_masking_v2_colab.ipynb read the commands from this file's description; tests/test_exp040_plan.py holds them against exp-020's and exp-014's recorded commands.
why: The thesis's masking result (typed > uniform > raw) is v1 prior work, never re-run in v2, and none of its 15 tests survives Holm (docs/analysis/2026-08-20-v1-masking-and-retrieval-significance.json task_a_masking.holm_bonferroni; writing-audit (d) rank 1). exp-040 measures the three masking modes on the current fixed method.

pool.fields_present: question, question_masked_typed, question_masked_uniform, few_shot_decomposition_musique on 2000/2000 rows (checked on the laptop copy 2026-11-27). The pool's masked fields are pre-computed (ADR 0003: queries masked at lookup, the pool never re-masked).

exp014_typed_artifact.note: exp-020's retrieval input. Built with --mode typed, so it carries typed_top_k only: the raw and uniform arms cannot read it, hence the rebuild below.

retrieval_build._note: Notebook stage 'retrieval' (run.sh retrieval). exp-014's two commands (experiments/exp-014/config.json deliverable_2_commands) with exactly three changes: --mode all instead of --mode typed (raw, typed and uniform top-20 lists in one file), --no-cache (pool embeddings are computed from the pinned pool, never read from a cache whose key carries another machine's path), and exp-040 output paths. CPU, as exp-014 ran. The artifact's sha256 is PINNED at first build: run.sh writes it to runs/exp-040/retrieval/PINNED_SHA256 (on Drive) and every later step refuses a different file; run_decomposer --resume refuses a different retrieval sha256 as well.
retrieval_build.check: experiments/exp-040/check_retrieval.py -> runs/exp-040/retrieval/check.json: 600 rows, 600 distinct ids equal to the exp-014 artifact's ids, 200/200/200 by hop prefix, >= 5 candidates per mode per row; typed exemplar identity vs exp-014 (ordered top-5 pool_id lists, per query); top-5 overlap between modes (descriptive).

typed_rerun.role: the typed arm: exp-020's exact command re-run on the same Colab GPU (exp-037's same-machine convention, ADR 0043 item 7). Also the hardware control against stored exp-020.
typed_rerun.retrieval_mode_note: not passed: configs/decomposer_musique.json retrieval.mode is typed, as in exp-020's command

raw.role: raw questions on both sides of the bi-encoder and the cross-encoder

uniform.role: every NER entity replaced by one [MASK] placeholder on both sides

typed_rebuilt.role: CONDITIONAL. Typed mode read from the rebuilt artifact. Runs only if check.json typed_identity.identical < 600, i.e. if the rebuild did not reproduce exp-014's typed exemplars for every query; then the typed arm the primary pairs use is this one (same artifact build as raw/uniform), and typed_rerun stays as the hardware control.

typed_comparator_rule._note: Declared before any run. Which run is 'typed' in the primary pairs.
typed_comparator_rule.if_typed_identity_600_of_600: typed_rerun. Its prompts are byte-identical to what typed mode on the rebuilt artifact would give (same exemplars, same order), so the arms differ only in --retrieval-mode.
typed_comparator_rule.otherwise: typed_rebuilt (same artifact build as raw and uniform); typed_rerun is then reported as context and as the hardware control.

canary._note: Before each arm's full decode: the same command on the first 20 rows of its retrieval file (--sample-size 20 --allow-unpinned-eval-set, own output root runs/exp-040/canary/<arm>), then the output-health check on those 20 rows. A canary is not an experiment arm and is never compared.

output_health_gate._note: Applied to every canary and every full decode by experiments/exp-040/check_health.py; a failure stops that arm and is recorded in runs/exp-040/<arm>/HEALTH_FAILED.json. Thresholds are pre-declared here and ARBITRARY beyond what is stated: exp-020 recorded rows_with_empty_decomposition 0 (experiments/exp-020/metrics.json); the 1%-of-rows ceiling exists to stop a broken run (NaN logits, a wrong template) without failing an arm that legitimately leaves one or two rows empty.
output_health_gate.max_rows_at_max_new_tokens_note: arbitrary; exp-020 used max_new_tokens 1024 and a step decomposition is ~30-80 tokens, so many rows at the cap means runaway generation

comparisons._note: experiments/exp-040/compare.py (CPU). Statistics are exp-029's run_pair (the evaluator's own paired bootstrap, exact McNemar, paired t; experiments/exp-029/reanalysis.py) and Holm beside the uncorrected verdict (ADR 0009, 0036). Fixed here before any exp-040 p-value exists (ADR 0036 item 5).

uniform_vs_raw.note: completes v1's ordering; uncorrected, in no family

typed_rerun_vs_exp020_stored.note: hardware control; uncorrected, in no family

typed_rebuilt_vs_typed_rerun.note: only if typed_rebuilt ran: the effect of the rebuild's differing typed exemplars; context

exp020_stored.note: exp-020 read through exp-032's re-parse (ADR 0039 cross-parser rule; 24/600 rows changed by the re-parse), because exp-040 runs on the ADR 0039 parser

comparisons.holm_p_basis: ADR 0036 item 3: exact McNemar p for break_exact_match, hop_count_exact_match, under/over_decomposition; paired-t p for sari, ged, chain_validity; bootstrap CI beside it, disagreements disclosed.
comparisons.pre_declared_direction: none. v1 reported typed > uniform > raw before correction; exp-040 tests both primary pairs two-sided and reports every term.

hardware_control.reproduced_if: typed_rerun's recorded decomposition equals runs/exp-032/exp-020/reparse/results.json's decomposition as exact strings for 600/600 query ids
hardware_control.consequence: Primary pairs are unaffected either way (all arms on one machine). If not reproduced, any statement setting exp-040 numbers beside stored v2 numbers carries the hardware caveat.

comparisons.wording: ADR 0036 item 4: non-significance is 'not distinguishable', never 'equal'. A claim that masking helps is made only for cells that survive Holm in F1/F2.

gpu.measured_reference: exp-020 peak 4,818 MiB (nvidia-smi, own pid) on the RTX 3090
gpu.requirement_text: any CUDA GPU with >= 12 GiB; the Colab runner uses an A100 (40 GB), possibly shared with another experiment

wall_clock_estimate._note: ESTIMATES, not measurements, for an A100 used by this notebook alone; a GPU shared with another job is slower. Bases: exp-020 decode 2,526 s on the RTX 3090 (4-bit, 600 queries, few-shot prompts); exp-014 built its typed artifact on a 64-thread CPU in 62.5 s (similarity) + 51.5 s (rerank). 4-bit decoding at batch 1 is bandwidth-bound; an A100 should be at or below the 3090 time (exp-037 README). The rebuild does three modes instead of one on Colab's ~12 vCPUs.
